diagnostic_evidence.quote: Finally, we extend these results to noncompactly supported measures with sufficient decay.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the approximation rates are generalized to non-compact measures. The only result, cor:added-1, gives a bound with a fixed additive eps. That eps is tied, through the decay hypotheses, to a fixed R. As N grows, the bound tends to eps, not 0, so no rate in N (not even convergence) is proved. Letting eps go to 0 forces R to infinity, and then N(B_R,V_0) grows; this trade-off is never analysed. No N-term count for the approximation of the non-compact measure is stated either.

failure_location.quote: In the last section, we generalize the approximation rates to non-compactly supported measures with suitable tail decay.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either weaken the claim to 'approximation up to eps', or add a quantitative tail assumption and choose R=R(N), balancing eps(R) against N(B_R,V_0)^{1/d}N^{-1/d} to obtain an actual rate.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised rate result for non-compactly supported measures is not supported; only an approximation up to a non-vanishing eps is shown.
issues.title: Claimed extension of approximation rates to non-compact measures is not established
issues.why_classification: Keeping the advertised content needs a new, contained optimization argument. Merely rewording loses the claimed rate result.

issues.failure_explanation: The display bounds E[W_p(mu,mu_N)] by roughly N^{-p/d} when p<d/2. For p>1 this is o(N^{-1/d}). That contradicts the paper's own statements that N-point approximations of absolutely continuous measures satisfy W_p = Omega(N^{-1/d}), i.e. Theta(N^{-1/d}). The displayed rates must refer to E[W_p^p], not E[W_p].
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the bound for E[W_p^p] (equivalently, take p-th roots of the rates).
issues.overall_effect: The literature comparison underlying the 'matches known rates' claim is misstated for p>1.
issues.title: Quoted Fournier-Guillin bound is internally inconsistent with the cited lower bounds
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction of a background statement and leaves no result of the paper affected.

issues.failure_explanation: The cited fact is quoted as requiring T⊂K. It is applied with T=V_0 and K=B_R for arbitrary R. Nothing ensures V_0⊂B_R; this fails, for example, when R<rad(V_0).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use submultiplicativity: N(B_R,hV_0) ≤ N(B_R,V_0) N(V_0,hV_0), together with N(V_0,hV_0) ≤ (1+2/h)^d for symmetric V_0. This needs no inclusion.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the lemma's proof is valid only when V_0⊂B_R.
issues.title: Covering-number fact applied outside its stated hypothesis T ⊂ K
issues.why_classification: A standard two-line replacement argument gives the same statement unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: For p≥1, (a−b)^p ≤ a^p − b^p, so |x| ≥ |hλ| − r does not give |x|^p ≥ |hλ|^p − r^p. The lower bound with absolute value in EQN:xbound is also false when |hλ| < r. The claim (i) itself fails. Take d=1, Λ=Z, V_0=[-1/2,1/2), h=1, p=2 and μ=δ_{3/2}. Then the left side is 4, but the right side is 1/4+9/4=2.5. The same example falsifies the displayed moment bound for μ_h.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (i) by Σ|hλ|^p μ(V_{hλ}) ≤ 2^{p-1}(M_p(μ)+h^p rad(V_0)^p). This follows from |hλ| ≤ |x|+h rad(V_0) and convexity; then adjust the constants in the two moment estimates.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit moment bounds in the proofs that μ_h and ν_h lie in W_p are false for p>1. Finiteness of these moments, which is all the theorems state, remains true.
issues.title: Lemma estimate (i) is false for p>1; invalid inequality |x|^p ≥ |hλ|^p − rad^p
issues.why_classification: The fix is a short, routine replacement of the bound. Downstream results need only finiteness, so all substantive claims survive.

issues.failure_explanation: h ≤ 1 holds only when N ≥ 3^d N(B_R,V_0), yet the theorem allows every N. LEM:CoveringNumber (3^d h^{-d} bound) and THM:InfiniteLatticeDirac are stated only for h∈(0,1]. The term-count claim can then fail. Take Λ=0.02Z×50Z, so N(B_1,V_0)=100, and N=1. Then h=30 and the cells are 0.6-wide strips. The uniform measure on B_{0.9} charges 3 cells, which exceeds N=1.

failure_location.quote: set $h=3\left(\frac{\mc{N}}{N}\right)^{\frac1d}$. Then $\mu_h = \sum_{\lambda\in \Lambda} \mu(V_{h\lambda})\delta_{h\lambda}$ is an at most $N$-term approximation

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis N ≥ 3^d N(B_R,V_0), equivalently h ≤ 1, to the theorem and its piecewise-constant and non-compact analogues.
issues.overall_effect: The 'at most N terms' guarantee is false for small N.
issues.title: N-term theorem stated for all N, but its proof requires h ≤ 1
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard parameter restriction preserves the method, the rate and the asymptotic scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: let $\mc{N}(K,T)$ be the minimal number of translates of $T$ it takes to cover $K$

issues.failure_explanation: The number of terms of μ_h equals the number of lattice cells V_{hλ} meeting supp μ. The covering number N(B_R,hV_0), however, allows arbitrarily positioned translates, so it can be smaller. Take d=1, Λ=Z, h=1/2, R=1. Then N(B_1,hV_0)=4, but the uniform measure on [-0.9,0.9] charges 5 cells, k=-2,...,2. The first inequality of the proof is therefore false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Each translate of hV_0 meets at most 3^d lattice cells, since those cells lie in a translate of 3hV_0. Hence #terms ≤ 3^d N(B_R,hV_0) ≤ 9^d h^{-d} N. Take h=9(N/N)^{1/d}, giving the bound 9 rad(V_0) N^{1/d} N^{-1/d}.
issues.overall_effect: The N-term guarantee, with its stated constants, is unproved.
issues.title: Number of lattice cells charged by μ is not bounded by the covering number
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a new counting lemma and changes the explicit constants of the theorem. The O(N^{-1/d}) rate survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: let $\Lambda_N = (N^{-\frac1d}\Z)^d$ with Voronoi cells $(V_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda_N}$. Then $\mu_N = \sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_N}\mu(V_{\lambda})\delta_{\lambda}$ is an at most $N$-term approximation

issues.failure_explanation: The cells are centred at lattice points, which include the origin. They tile the cube with N cells only when N^{1/d} is an odd integer. For d=1, N=2, the cells are [k/2−1/4, k/2+1/4), and the uniform measure on [-0.45,0.45] charges 3 cells. For d=2, N=2, nine cells are charged. The 'at most N' (and 'N-term') claim therefore fails for most N.

failure_location.quote: Setting $h=N^{-\frac1d}$ yields $N$ cubes of length $N^{-\frac1d}$ in the unit cube

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restrict to N=n^d with n odd, or use a half-shifted grid when n is even. For general N, use the largest admissible n with n^d ≤ N; this adjusts the constant.
issues.overall_effect: The term-count guarantees of both pixel corollaries are false in general. The rate bounds themselves remain valid.
issues.title: Grid (N^{-1/d}Z)^d does not give ≤ N cells on the unit cube
issues.why_classification: The repair restricts N or alters the construction and constant. A comparable result survives.

issues.failure_explanation: The integral equals 1/R, so I_1<ε^p/3 is not shown for R<1. The theorem then fails. Take p=1 and density equal to the maximum allowed off B_R, with the remaining mass as an atom at 0. Then I_1=ε/(6R), and W_1(μ,μ̂) ≥ I_1 > ε for R<1/2 (for example R=0.1, ε=0.01).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume R ≥ 1, or put an extra factor min(1,R) in the density hypothesis.
issues.overall_effect: W_p(μ,μ̂)<ε is false for small R, so the non-compact corollary is unreliable there.
issues.title: Density tail estimate I_1 uses ∫_R^∞ r^{-2} dr ≤ 1, false for R<1
issues.why_classification: A local hypothesis adjustment preserves the conclusion and the method.

issues.failure_explanation: With θ=1−{R}∈(0,1), the series is Σ_{m≥0}(m+θ)^{-2}, which exceeds π²/6 and blows up as θ→0. Concrete counterexample: d=2, p=1, R=1.9, ε=10^{-3}, μ=(1−m)δ_0+mσ with σ uniform on |x|=2 and m=2000ε/π². This μ satisfies hypotheses (1)–(3). Yet W_1(μ,μ̂) ≥ ∫(|x|−R)_+ dμ = 0.1m ≈ 20ε > ε.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume R∈N (or replace R by ⌈R⌉), or change the hypothesis to use (j+1−R)^p(j+1−⌊R⌋)^2.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem and the non-compact corollary fail for non-integer R.
issues.title: Shell series bound ≤ π²/6 fails for non-integer R; theorem false
issues.why_classification: A standard local adjustment of the hypothesis restores the stated conclusion with the same proof.
